steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Simple time divides beats into 2 (2/4, 3/4, 4/4); compound time divides into 3 (6/8, 9/8, 12/8) — the feel is fundamentally different. | Key Fact: Syncopation places emphasis on off-beats or weak beats — it creates rhythmic tension and is central to jazz, blues and popular music. | Key Fact: Polyrhythm is two or more conflicting rhythmic patterns played simultaneously — common in African and Caribbean music traditions. | Key Fact: Hemiola creates a temporary shift of metre (e.g. feeling 2 groups of 3 as 3 groups of 2) — used from Renaissance to pop music.

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Describe how rhythm metre and tempo are used in a piece of music you have studied. Use musical vocabulary. | Compare how two different pieces use rhythm metre and tempo. Explain the effect in each case. | How could you use rhythm metre and tempo in your own composition or performance? Explain your choices.
